paragraphs.title: Sarcasm toward Conventional Wisdom and the Reversal of Reality

answers: He says that he also has understanding
He says he has no understanding
He asks them to teach him to read
easy.explanation: Job says, “I have understanding as well as you; I am not inferior to you.”
easy.q: How does Job respond to the wisdom of his friends?

answers: He is always honored
He is mocked and laughed to scorn
He is made a ruler
easy.explanation: Job describes himself as one mocked by his neighbour and laughed to scorn.
easy.q: How is the suffering person treated according to Job?

answers: The poor only
The righteous only
Robbers and those who provoke God
easy.explanation: Job says, “The tabernacles of robbers prosper,” and those who provoke God are secure.
easy.q: Who may live in peace and security according to these verses?

answers: Because he also has understanding and knows such things
Because they say nothing at all
Because they speak only about animals
medium.explanation: Job says that he has understanding as well as they do, and asks, “who knoweth not such things as these?”
medium.q: Why are Job’s friends’ words not new to him?

answers: A light guiding travelers
A person regarded with contempt
A tool used to build a tent
medium.explanation: The comparison describes someone who is despised by those who are at ease.
medium.q: What does the expression “a lamp despised” describe in context?

answers: The sufferer is mocked, while robbers may prosper and be secure
The sufferer is wealthy, while robbers are homeless
The sufferer is a ruler, while robbers are judges
medium.explanation: Job points to the apparent reversal in which the sufferer is ridiculed while robbers prosper.
medium.q: What contrast does Job present between the suffering person and robbers?

answers: To agree that all their words are new and correct
To accept their explanation of his suffering
To criticize their confidence in conventional wisdom
challenge.explanation: Job sarcastically claims that he also has understanding and that their wisdom is not superior or new.
challenge.q: What is the purpose of Job’s sarcasm toward his friends?

answers: Outward prosperity does not necessarily prove righteousness
All robbers are righteous
Only sufferers understand God
challenge.explanation: The passage shows wicked people enjoying security, challenging a simple view that visible prosperity always proves righteousness.
challenge.q: What conclusion follows from the example of robbers and those who provoke God?

answers: It shows that he wants to leave the conversation
It emphasizes that he is not inferior to his friends in understanding
It proves that he is older than they are
challenge.explanation: Job immediately adds, “I am not inferior to you,” asserting intellectual equality.
challenge.q: How does “I have understanding as well as you” strengthen Job’s argument?

paragraphs.title: Creation Testifies That Everything Is in God’s Hand

answers: To kings only
To the beasts, birds, earth, and fishes
To counselors and judges
easy.explanation: Job tells them to ask the beasts, the fowls of the air, the earth, and the fishes of the sea.
easy.q: To whom does Job direct his friends to learn about God’s power?

answers: All these things in creation
The birds only
The sea only
easy.explanation: Job asks who does not know that “the hand of the LORD hath wrought this.”
easy.q: What has the hand of the LORD wrought?

answers: Only human possessions
Only the wisdom of elders
The soul of every living thing and the breath of mankind
easy.explanation: The verse says that the soul of every living thing and the breath of all mankind are in God’s hand.
easy.q: What is in God’s hand according to the passage?

answers: They all testify to God’s power
They all need human counselors
They all live securely like the robbers
medium.explanation: Job points to every part of creation as evidence of the LORD’s workmanship.
medium.q: What do the beasts, birds, earth, and fishes have in common in Job’s argument?

answers: They will lead you along a road
They will instruct you
They will hide things from you
medium.explanation: Job personifies creation as something from which people can learn about God.
medium.q: What does “they shall teach thee” mean in this context?

answers: They say that humans are not part of the world
They declare that life and breath are held in God’s hand
They describe only human food
medium.explanation: After mentioning creation, Job speaks of the soul of every living thing and the breath of mankind.
medium.q: How do these verses connect creation with human life?

answers: To show that people can discern and examine things
To describe a great feast
To explain how fish swim
challenge.explanation: The ear tests words and the mouth tastes food, illustrating human powers of examination and discernment.
challenge.q: Why does Job mention the ear trying words and the mouth tasting food?

answers: The aged are described as lacking all understanding
Length of days is associated with wisdom and understanding
The aged are said not to be alive
challenge.explanation: Job says, “With the ancient is wisdom; and in length of days understanding.”
challenge.q: What relationship between age and wisdom appears in verse 12?

answers: Only humans recognize God’s power
Both nature and humanity depend on God’s power
Understanding has no connection with life
challenge.explanation: Job presents creation, life, breath, discernment, wisdom, and understanding as matters under God’s authority.
challenge.q: What idea is suggested by the movement from nature to human understanding?

paragraphs.title: Divine Wisdom and Power Govern Reality

answers: Wisdom, strength, counsel, and understanding
Wealth and honor only
Physical strength only
easy.explanation: The verse says, “With him is wisdom and strength, he hath counsel and understanding.”
easy.q: What does God possess according to verse 13?

answers: Build only
Break down and build again
Open doors only
easy.explanation: Job says, “he breaketh down, and it cannot be built again.”
easy.q: What can God do according to these verses?

answers: He withholds them or sends them out
He drinks them
He hides them from the earth
easy.explanation: The passage says that God withholds the waters and also sends them out.
easy.q: What does God do with the waters?

answers: They enable him to determine whether things are built or broken down
They prevent him from acting
They belong only to human counselors
medium.explanation: God’s wisdom and strength are presented as the basis of his authority to alter circumstances.
medium.q: How are God’s wisdom and strength related to his rule over circumstances?

answers: Both the one who is deceived and the one who deceives remain under his authority
Only builders belong to God
Only righteous judges belong to God
medium.explanation: Job declares that both the deceived and the deceiver are within God’s sovereignty.
medium.q: What does “the deceived and the deceiver are his” indicate?

answers: Counsellors, judges, kings, and princes
Fishermen, farmers, and shepherds only
Beasts, birds, and fishes
medium.explanation: The verses mention counsellors, judges, kings, princes, and the mighty.
medium.q: Which groups are included among those whom God leads or overturns?

answers: God acts in only one way
God controls both destruction and restriction
God never changes circumstances
challenge.explanation: The language presents God as sovereign both over what is broken and over what is prevented from opening.
challenge.q: What do the paired actions “he breaketh down” and “he shutteth up” reveal?

answers: The waters can be withheld or released by God
The waters are unrelated to the world
The waters represent only the wisdom of elders
challenge.explanation: Job describes God as able to stop the waters and send them out so that they overturn the earth.
challenge.q: Why does the reference to the waters strengthen the theme of divine rule?

answers: It extends only over nature
It extends only over government
It includes nature, counselors, judges, kings, and mighty people
challenge.explanation: The passage moves from buildings and waters to political and social leaders, showing comprehensive authority.
challenge.q: How broad is God’s authority in these verses?

paragraphs.title: The Reversal of the Status of the Powerful and Wise

answers: Priests, the mighty, the aged, and princes
Animals only
The poor only
easy.explanation: The passage refers to priests, the mighty, the aged, princes, and other people of status.
easy.q: Over whom can God act according to these verses?

answers: Their speech
Their houses
Their clothing only
easy.explanation: The verse says, “He removeth away the speech of the trusty.”
easy.q: What can God remove from the trustworthy?

answers: Greater honor
Contempt
Priestly authority
easy.explanation: The verse says, “He poureth contempt upon princes.”
easy.q: What does God pour upon princes?

answers: Their understanding is taken away
More days are added to them
They are made kings
medium.explanation: Job says that God “taketh away the understanding of the aged.”
medium.q: How is the condition of the aged described as being changed?

answers: People possessing strength or power
Blind people
People without homes
medium.explanation: The term describes those who are strong or powerful.
medium.q: What does “the mighty” refer to in this context?

answers: Both are examples of impairing the abilities of people with status
Both are acts of construction
Both describe animals
medium.explanation: The verses describe God removing speech from the trusty and understanding from the aged.
medium.q: What connection exists between removing speech and taking away understanding?

answers: No human status is beyond God’s power to reverse
Only priests are important
The aged are stronger than everyone else
challenge.explanation: The list emphasizes that God can overturn the condition of people from many respected classes.
challenge.q: What is the main idea in the list of priests, the mighty, the aged, and princes?

answers: It describes the weakening of power that once seemed secure
It describes a military victory by princes
It explains how houses are built
challenge.explanation: The statement continues the theme of God diminishing the strength of powerful people.
challenge.q: How does “he weakeneth the strength of the mighty” fit the passage?

answers: Both show the loss of honor or ability once regarded as secure
Both praise human leaders
Both concern only natural phenomena
challenge.explanation: Job shows God removing speech, understanding, honor, and strength from respected people.
challenge.q: What relationship exists between contempt upon princes and the loss of understanding among the aged?

paragraphs.title: Revealing the Hidden and Confounding Nations and Leaders

answers: Deep things and the shadow of death
Only the faces of kings
The tabernacles of robbers
easy.explanation: The verse says that God discovers deep things out of darkness and brings the shadow of death to light.
easy.q: What does God bring out of darkness?

answers: Increase or destroy them
Enrich them only
Lead them only to the temple
easy.explanation: The passage says, “He increaseth the nations, and destroyeth them.”
easy.q: What can God do to nations?

answers: As finding a clear path
As groping in darkness and staggering like a drunken man
As teaching everyone else
easy.explanation: They grope in the dark without light and are made to stagger like a drunken man.
easy.q: How are the leaders of the earth described at the end of the passage?

answers: He can increase, destroy, enlarge, or straiten them
He can punish them only
He can give them wisdom only
medium.explanation: The verses describe God increasing, destroying, enlarging, and straitening nations.
medium.q: What different outcomes can God determine for nations?

answers: He hides things that are already clear
He brings hidden and profound things into light
He leads people toward the sea
medium.explanation: The expression describes God revealing what was hidden in darkness.
medium.q: What does “discovereth deep things out of darkness” mean?

answers: God takes away their understanding and causes them to wander
They receive too much wisdom
There is too much light
medium.explanation: The passage says God takes away the heart, or understanding, of the leaders and causes them to wander.
medium.q: Why do the chief people of the earth wander without a way?

answers: God can reveal what is hidden while also removing leaders’ ability to understand their way
Both prove that God does not act in the world
Both concern only the growth of nations
challenge.explanation: The passage presents God as sovereign over both hidden knowledge and the understanding of rulers.
challenge.q: What connection exists between revealing deep things and confusing leaders?

answers: Stability and confidence
Confusion and loss of direction
Wisdom and experience
challenge.explanation: A drunken person staggers without direction, symbolizing the leaders’ confusion.
challenge.q: What does the image of a drunken man emphasize?

answers: The fate of nations is subject to God’s increase, destruction, enlargement, and restraint
Nations determine everything without divine influence
God concerns himself only with private individuals
challenge.explanation: Job says that God can increase, destroy, enlarge, and straiten the nations.
challenge.q: How does the passage describe the relationship between God’s power and the fate of nations?
